parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation or traveller-facing restriction is documented anywhere in the record; same-sex conduct legal since 2001, a constitutional non-discrimination guarantee since 2010, and a 2015 marriage ordinance expressly covering gender identity signal an accepting institutional climate. No dated incident of anti-trans violence or discrimination exists. The dossier is thin: nothing addresses screening, facilities, detention, healthcare, or social reception, and a ~50-resident community offers no anonymity, so a visibly trans visitor is highly visible with unknown-but-likely-harmless consequences. Extrapolating from the structural signals (decriminalisation, anti-discrimination charter, unanimous equality legislation, no record of relief denied or hostility shown), risk resolves toward the reduced/low boundary, not the midpoint. Silent record is a moderately positive signal given functioning rule-of-law parentage; unresolved facility/custody questions and total absence of documented trans-specific acceptance or protection keep it below 0.85.
